# Storage, ids and timestamps: is this moment mine?

## What this region is

The low-level ground every hivemind module stands on: one cached bun:sqlite database per project under HIVEMIND_BASE, the {prefix}_{6hex}[_{label}] id scheme, and the local yyyy/mm/dd hh:mm:ss TZ timestamp format.

## What it exists for

- Get a working database handle for a project
- Prepare a project's hivemind database from an MCP client
- Find where a project's state lives on disk
- Get or check a hivemind id
- Mint ids for plans, tasks, subtasks and events
- Read the parts of an existing id
- Write, read or age a stored timestamp
- Format part or all of a Date

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- I'll insert the event row and bump the sequence counter myself → event-log
- mark agents dead when their last-seen time is older than the lease → agents-and-liveness
- create a plan and its tasks from the markdown file → plans-and-tasks
- run hivemind init so the repo gets its database and hooks → claude-code-integration
- use the git repo's name as the project name → git-and-worktrees
